results.preview: Direct answer: Scripture speaks of Jesus’ resurrection and of the resurrection of the dead in ordered witness: a first resurrection of the righteous who reign with Christ, and the rest of the dead afterward (Revelation 20; John 5; Daniel 12) — not a single collapsed answer. Scripture witnesses: Revelation 20:4-6; Revelation 20:5; John 5:28-29; Daniel 12:2.

Direct answer: In the first resurrection, God’s people who are Christ’s are raised to life and reign with Him; Revelation 20:4-6 calls this the first resurrection, with 1 Thessalonians 4 and 1 Corinthians 15 describing the gathering of the dead in Christ. Scripture witnesses: Revelation 20:4-6; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-17; 1 Corinthians 15:51-54; John 5:28-29.

After they are raised in the first resurrection, God's people will reign with Christ. Revelation 20:4-6 describes this clearly, stating that those who are resurrected will live and reign with Him for a thousand years. Additionally, passages like 1 Thessalonians 4:17 indicate that they will be caught up to meet the Lord in the air, emphasizing the gathering and transformation of believers at that time.

Direct answer: Revelation 20:5 says the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished; that is distinct from the first resurrection of those who reign with Christ. Scripture witnesses: Revelation 20:5; Revelation 20:4-6; John 5:28-29; Daniel 12:2.

Direct answer: Scripture does not teach that the same first-resurrection saints are raised again in the second; Revelation 20 distinguishes the first resurrection from the rest of the dead who live after the thousand years, and John 5 / Daniel 12 speak of resurrection unto life and unto judgment. Scripture witnesses: Revelation 20:4-6; Revelation 20:5; John 5:28-29; Daniel 12:2.

In the first resurrection, after God's people are raised, they will reign with Christ for a thousand years. This reign is described in Revelation 20:4-6, which states that they will live and rule with Him. Additionally, they will be caught up to meet the Lord in the air (1 Thessalonians 4:17), signifying a transformation and gathering of believers during this time.

Scripture speaks of Jesus’ resurrection and of the resurrection of the dead in ordered witness: a first resurrection of the righteous who reign with Christ, and the rest of the dead afterward (Revelation 20; John 5; Daniel 12) — not a single collapsed answer. (Revelation 20:4-6; Revelation 20:5)
Direct answer: The seventh day is the Sabbath established at creation and commanded in Scripture. Scripture witnesses: Genesis 2:2-3; Exodus 20:8-11; leviticus 23:1-3; Isaiah 58:13-14.

Direct answer: The dead know nothing, their thoughts perish, and Scripture describes death as sleep until resurrection. Scripture witnesses: Ecclesiastes 9:5; Ecclesiastes 9:10; Psalm 146:4; John 11:11-14.
